system:
You extract quantitative facts about one clinical trial programme from one document.

Rules:
- Extract only facts stated in THIS document. Never use outside knowledge.
- Every fact needs "quote": an exact, verbatim span copied from the document (8-300 characters) that contains the number. Quotes are machine-checked; paraphrases are discarded.
- Placebo-adjusted values are preferred. If a value is within-arm (not placebo-adjusted), set attrs.placebo_adjusted=false.
- Units: keep the unit the document uses; put it in "unit".
- Other trials of the same investigational drug (phase 2, dose-finding, other populations, combination arms) belong
  to the programme: extract their facts too, and put the trial's name in attrs.trial when the document gives it.
- Return {"facts": []} only if the document reports no results for the investigational drug.

Allowed keys:
  n_randomized, median_followup, primary_endpoint, inclusion_threshold, planned_events, assumed_rrr, power,
  alpha, stopped_early, events_treatment, events_control, events_total, hr, ci_low, ci_high, p_value,
  biomarker_change, baseline_level, sbp_change, safety_signal, readout_statement

For biomarker_change and baseline_level, attrs must include: biomarker (one of LDL-C, non-HDL-C, apoB, HDL-C,
Lp(a), triglycerides, hsCRP, IL-6, Lp-PLA2 activity, sPLA2-IIA, SBP, other), phase (phase2 or phase3),
timepoint, method (assay or "not stated"), placebo_adjusted (true/false), dose (if stated).
For biomarker_change give "value" as the change (negative = reduction) and state in attrs.kind whether it is
"percent" or "absolute".

Return JSON only:
{"facts": [{"key": "...", "value": <number or string>, "unit": "...", "attrs": {...}, "quote": "..."}]}

--- DOCUMENT TEXT ---
ClinicalTrials.gov record NCT01841944 (OMEMI)
Title: Omega-3 Fatty Acids in Elderly Patients With Acute Myocardial Infarction
Official title: Giving Omega-3 Fatty Acids to Elderly Patients Diagnosed With Acute Myocardial Infarction to Investigate the Effect on Cardiovascular Morbidity and Mortality
Sponsor: Oslo University Hospital
Phase: NA
Conditions: Myocardial Infarction; Heart Failure; Myocardial Revascularization; Atrial Fibrillation
Interventions: Pikasol (DRUG); Corn oil (OTHER)
Start date: 2012-11
Enrollment: 1027 (ACTUAL)
Primary outcome(s): Combined total mortality, first event of non-fatal myocardial infarction, stroke, revascularization or hospital admission for new or worsened heart failure. [24months]
Eligibility criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients with acute myocardial infarction discharged from hospital alive

Exclusion Criteria:

* Being part of another randomized trial
* Documented intolerance for omega-3 fatty acids
* Additional disease state that is thought to be incompatible with compliance to the study drugs
* Additional disease state thought to reduce survival for the follow-up time of 2 years
Brief summary: The aim of the present study is to investigate the possible effects of supplementation with 1.8 g/day of n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids on cardiovascular morbidity and mortality during a follow-up period of 2 years in an elderly population after having experienced an acute myocardial infarction. The hypothesis is that this supplementation on top of modern therapy will reduce the combined cardiovascular end-point of death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, stroke, revascularizations or hospitalization for new or worsened heart failure with at least 30%.
--- END ---
